# The Fortran 90 end-to-end programs

`docs/planning/PHASE-99 - Fortran 90.md`'s Decision 16 and subtask 6: each
`name.f90` is a program in free source form and `name.out` what running it
prints at the terminal, followed by SHOW SYMBOL's line for `$STATUS`. A
program that reads the terminal has `name.in`, the lines typed (not echoed).
`TestFortran90Programs` (`internal/console/fortranprograms_test.go`) runs
them as `TestFortranPrograms` runs `testdata/fortran`'s: each source copied
to a volume as `NAME.F90`, which FORTRAN reads in free form with `/F90` by its
type; FORTRAN, MACRO, and LINK must say nothing; compiled `/NOOPTIMIZE`,
`/OPTIMIZE`, and both again `/RECURSIVE`; with paging off, and on for those
in `fortran90PagingPrograms` (all of them so far).

`modules/` holds programs of several files, a directory each, run by
`TestFortran90Modules` once per line of its `links.txt`, as
`testdata/fortran/modules`'s are. Its sources may be of either form: `.f90`
free, `.for` fixed.

The expected output is worked by hand from the standard (ISO/IEC 1539:1991)
and the *VAX FORTRAN Language Reference Manual* for what FTNRTL prints, never
copied from a run. `testdata/fortran/gfortran/compare.py` is the witness: it
builds each program here with `gfortran -std=f95` and compares its output
with the `.out` file. A difference is read against the standard, and neither
compiler is assumed right. To add a program, add its files here and its row
to `fortran90PagingPrograms` and to `compare.py`'s `PROGRAMS90` if it is
portable; this directory's `.gitignore` keeps `*.out` from the repository's
own rule.

The first programs (Phase 99) are FORTRAN-77, with DEC's END DO and DO WHILE,
in free form with Fortran 90's spellings; each later phase of the program adds
its own.

| Program | What it exercises |
| ------- | ----------------- |
| `spellings.f90` | `==`, `/=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` beside the old spellings; character constants between quotation marks or apostrophes, each doubled inside its own kind, in expressions and in FORMAT statements; `!` comments, and a `!` or `&` inside a constant; `;`; a constant, a number, and a statement continued with `&`, over a comment line; B, O, and Z constants in DATA; `END PROGRAM`, `END FUNCTION`, `END SUBROUTINE` with names |
| `squares.f90` | DO ... END DO, DO WHILE, a labeled DO ending at a CONTINUE, a block IF with ELSE IF written with `<`, `==`, and `>=`, labels first on their lines, DOUBLE PRECISION, quoted text in FORMAT statements |
| `strings.f90` | Concatenation, substrings, LEN, INDEX, ICHAR and CHAR, LLT, comparisons written with `<`, `==`, and `/=` of different lengths, passed-length dummies, a logical IF with a substring assignment |
| `layout.f90` | Free form's layout (the standard's 3.3.1): continuation over comment and blank lines, an `&` starting the next line or not, a character constant continued with its blanks, a label after a `;`, a DO loop on one line, GO TO, END DO, ELSE IF, END IF, and DOUBLE PRECISION with their blanks and without, keywords in either case, a line of 132 characters |
| `average.f90` | Terminal input in free form: an A edit and list-directed numbers until a negative one, by DO WHILE (`average.in`) |
| `declare.f90` | Fortran 90's declarations (Phase 100, subtask 3): `::` with PARAMETER, DIMENSION, SAVE, EXTERNAL, and INTENT; initial values given with `=`, one value for a whole array; a subroutine counting its calls in a variable an initialization makes SAVE; DIMENSION `::` and SAVE `::` as statements; CHARACTER\*(\*) PARAMETER |
| `kinds.f90` | Fortran 90's kinds (Phase 100, subtask 4): kind selectors on INTEGER, REAL, COMPLEX, LOGICAL, and CHARACTER, with `KIND=` and without, kinds named by PARAMETERs, `LEN=` and `KIND=` in both orders, kinds on constants of every type, a REAL(8) given a REAL's value and a REAL(8) constant's, a REAL(16) product, a function with a kind selector |
| `bytes.f90` | Fortran 90's INTEGER(1) (Phase 100, subtask 5): byte arithmetic, a byte beside INTEGER(2), INTEGER, and REAL, constants of kind 1, the generic functions of bytes (ABS, MAX, MIN, IAND, IOR, IEOR, ISHFT, NOT, SIGN, MOD, DIM) and INT, a power, a DO loop and subscripts of kind 1, an array in DATA, a byte argument and a byte function, and I, O, Z, list-directed, and internal I/O both ways |
| `cplx16.f90` | Fortran 90's COMPLEX(16) (Phase 100, subtask 7): an initial value and constants of kind 16, sums, differences, products, quotients (FTNRTL's FTN$DIVCH), negation, `==` and `/=`, a folded quotient equal to the computed one, one third to 33 digits, conversions from COMPLEX(8), REAL(16), and INTEGER and back, CMPLX with KIND=16, REAL, AIMAG, CONJG, INT, KIND, PRECISION, an array with subscripts, a dummy array, and a COMPLEX(16) function; printed by its parts, its I/O not there yet |
| `inquire.f90` | Fortran 90's kind and inquiry functions (Phase 100, subtask 6): SELECTED_INT_KIND, SELECTED_REAL_KIND, and KIND in PARAMETERs and executable statements; HUGE, TINY, EPSILON, DIGITS, PRECISION, RANGE, RADIX, MINEXPONENT, MAXEXPONENT, and BIT_SIZE of every integer kind, REAL, and a REAL(8) dummy; KIND= on INT, NINT, REAL, CMPLX, and LOGICAL; keyword arguments. The real model's lines are the VAX's, `compare.py`'s KNOWN gfortran's |
| `precise.f90` | A program portable to any Fortran 90 processor (Phase 100, subtask 8): its precision asked for by SELECTED_REAL_KIND and SELECTED_INT_KIND in each unit's PARAMETERs, constants with kinds, KIND= on NINT, INT, REAL, and CMPLX, IMPLICIT with a kind given by SELECTED_REAL_KIND, a kind named by KIND of a dummy, a RESULT variable, INTENT, a function passed as an argument; Newton's square root, Simpson's rule, a loan's payments, a quadratic's complex roots. The same on gfortran with no known difference |
| `forms.f90` | Declarations of every form Phase 100 compiles, in one program (subtask 8): `::` and the old statements side by side, attributes as attributes and as statements (VOLATILE, INTENT, AUTOMATIC, STATIC, OPTIONAL, TARGET, EXTERNAL, INTRINSIC, DIMENSION), DEC's `*n` beside kind selectors and after a name (`REAL(8) :: X*4`), IMPLICIT with kinds, `/clist/`, DATA, and `=`, PARAMETER both ways, COMMON and EQUIVALENCE of names declared with `::`, INTEGER\*1, BYTE, DOUBLE COMPLEX, and COMPLEX(16). DEC's forms keep it from gfortran's `-std=f95`, so it isn't in `compare.py` |
| `selects.f90` | Fortran 90's CASE construct (Phase 101, subtask 4), each form the compiler gives it: an INTEGER construct by a CASEL table (with an open range tested outside it), by a binary search, and by a chain; an INTEGER(2) selector; LOGICAL with DEFAULT; CHARACTER ranges of text by a chain, single characters of a substring found at run time by a search, and a concatenation of a passed-length dummy (a dynamic string, freed after the comparisons); a constant selector; CYCLE and EXIT of a named DO from inside CASE blocks. The same on gfortran |
| `tokens.f90` | A tokenizer by SELECT CASE on CHARACTER (Phase 101, subtask 5): lines read from the terminal until its end by a DO with no loop control (`tokens.in`), each token's class chosen by its first character (a binary search of twenty tests), two-character operators by a substring of run-time length, named loops left by EXIT and CYCLE from inside CASE blocks, a kind counted by a CASE construct on a passed-length dummy, a loop variable's value after EXIT. The same on gfortran |
| `loops.f90` | Fortran 90's DO constructs with EXIT and CYCLE (Phase 101, subtask 5), with the shapes the optimizer must keep right: a named EXIT out of two counted loops whose variables live in registers, CYCLE in a loop closed by AOBLEQ, a count kept through CYCLE counting down, a named CYCLE of the outer loop, DO with no loop control left at its top and at its bottom, DO WHILE with CYCLE, a labeled and named DO with CYCLE and EXIT from a CASE block, three named loops; each loop variable's value after its loop. The same on gfortran |
| `cases.f90` | Every form of INTEGER selection (Phase 101, subtask 5): `caseForm`'s thresholds on both sides (a table of four tests over 16 values, a chain over 17; seven sparse tests a chain, eight a search), a table of seven values, open ranges both sides of a table based at -2, an INTEGER(1) selector's ranges reaching its limits, a function's value as the selector, a named CASE construct inside another with names on its CASE statements, a GO TO to a labeled END SELECT. The same on gfortran |
| `examples.f90` | The standard's own examples of the IF, CASE, and DO constructs (8.1.2.3, 8.1.3.3, 8.1.4.5; Phase 101, subtask 5) in its capitals, made to run: SIGNUM, the balanced parentheses, the three equivalent fragments, several selections of one block, and DO examples 2 to 10 (a "DO WHILE + 1/2" loop, CYCLE in a nonblock DO passing over its terminal CALL, CYCLE in loops sharing a CONTINUE, zero-trip inner loops), unit IUN a scratch file, formatted then unformatted; a format given as a constant with `"…"` in it. The same on gfortran |
| `arrays.f90` | Fortran 90's array assignment (Phase 102, subtask 4): an elemental expression of whole arrays, a comparison into a LOGICAL array, a section moved to another array's section, a negative stride, a column and a row of a matrix, a scalar broadcast, extents known only when the program runs (one of them zero), a stride of 2, a CHARACTER array's substrings and its comparison, DOUBLE PRECISION and COMPLEX arrays, an adjustable dummy array whole and as a section; each result printed whole or by an implied DO. The same on gfortran |
| `overlap.f90` | Overlap in array assignments (Phase 102, subtask 5): sections read ahead (loops up) and behind (loops down) in either dimension and by a stride of 2, a section read both ways and a reversal through a temporary, an array an EQUIVALENCE puts in the target, an element of the target read once before the loops, a CHARACTER array's own element and substrings. The same on gfortran |
| `vectors.f90` | Vector subscripts (Phase 102, subtask 6): elements gathered and scattered by a vector, vectors computed from vectors, a vector beside a triplet, a vector of a vector, a permutation of an array's own elements through a temporary, an adjustable dummy vector. The same on gfortran |
| `constants.f90` | Array constants and constructors (Phase 102, subtask 7): array PARAMETERs, one by RESHAPE, SIZE and UBOUND as constants, an initialized array, elements read with subscripts not constant, sections and operations on constants folded, a constructor with an implied DO whose variable is its own, one stored straight into a section of run-time extent, one reading its own target, a constant vector subscript, a CHARACTER PARAMETER's section. The same on gfortran |
| `elements.f90` | Elemental intrinsic functions on arrays (Phase 102, subtask 8): ABS, MAX with a scalar, NINT, SQRT (MTHRTL's, for each element), MOD, BTEST, MERGE of numbers and of CHARACTER values, MIN on a matrix, ICHAR of a section of substrings, DBLE of a section. The same on gfortran |
| `reduce.f90` | Fortran 90's array functions (Phase 102, subtask 9): SUM, PRODUCT, MAXVAL, MINVAL whole, masked, and by DIM=; COUNT, ANY, ALL; MAXLOC and MINLOC, masked and finding nothing; an empty sum; DOT_PRODUCT of REAL and COMPLEX vectors; MATMUL both ways; TRANSPOSE; a vector divided by its sum; SIZE, SHAPE, LBOUND, UBOUND, and a sum by DIM= of an adjustable array. The same on gfortran |
| `where.f90` | WHERE (Phase 102, subtask 10): the statement and the construct, with and without ELSEWHERE; a first assignment that changes what the mask reads (the mask kept in a temporary); a mask one element behind the target (the loop runs down); two dimensions; INTEGER targets and a constructor's values; a value through a temporary under a mask; a WHERE statement as a logical IF's. The same on gfortran |
| `arrayio.f90` | Arrays in I/O lists (Phase 102, subtask 11): sections with strides, going down, and of two dimensions, written an element at a time; array expressions, an array constant and a section of one, constructors with implied DOs, and functions' array values; sections in an implied-DO list; CHARACTER sections with substrings and concatenation; reading into sections, one whose extent the same statement reads, one with a vector subscript, and a section's substrings (`arrayio.in`); sections in an internal file's lists and in unformatted records. The same on gfortran |
| `matrix.f90` | A matrix program (Phase 102, subtask 12): Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting in a subroutine on an adjustable dummy array, the pivot by MAXLOC of a section, rows swapped and reduced as sections of the same array (`A(I, K:N) = A(I, K:N) - F * A(K, K:N)`, no temporary), back substitution by DOT_PRODUCT of sections; the determinant as PRODUCT of a constructor; the inverse a column at a time, checked by MATMUL of a PARAMETER's row; an INTEGER Gram matrix by MATMUL and TRANSPOSE, its trace, sums by DIM=, and a cube by MATMUL into its own argument. The same on gfortran |
| `stats.f90` | A statistics program (Phase 102, subtask 12): twenty scores in an array PARAMETER; mean, variance, and standard deviation by SUM of array expressions; MINVAL, MAXVAL, MAXLOC, MINLOC; COUNT and SUM with masks; a histogram by COUNT, its bars by implied DOs; standard scores; a sort by MINLOC of a shrinking section; a moving average of overlapping sections, and the same in place; the scores RESHAPEd into a table, with SUM, MAXVAL, MINVAL, COUNT, ALL, and ANY by DIM=, and a correlation by DOT_PRODUCT. The same on gfortran |
| `smooth.f90` | Image smoothing with WHERE (Phase 102, subtask 12): a picture drawn a row at a time by MERGE of CHARACTER values, neighbors counted from eight sections, strays removed and a hole filled by WHERE statements, a weighted smoothing from five sections into another array and in place (through a temporary), three levels by a WHERE construct with ELSEWHERE into CHARACTER and INTEGER arrays, edges by a gradient of sections, and levels scaled by MAXVAL under a mask. The same on gfortran |
| `internal.f90` | Internal procedures of a main program (Phase 103, subtask 3): host association of variables, an initialized array, COMMON, and the host's IMPLICIT; a name an internal procedure declares hiding the host's, and one it uses alone its own; the host's I and STEPS, first used in its executable statements, changed by an internal procedure in its DO loop; an internal function typed by its own declaration and one by the host's IMPLICIT; a sibling calling a sibling; a RECURSIVE internal function with RESULT; a CHARACTER internal function; the host's TWICE hiding the file's external TWICE. The same on gfortran |
| `hosts.f90` | Internal procedures of subprograms (Phase 103, subtask 3): a subroutine's adjustable array, scalar, and CHARACTER\*(\*) dummies and its SAVE'd variable reached by its internal procedures; a REAL function's value and a CHARACTER function's (through its hidden argument) set by an internal subroutine. Compiled `/RECURSIVE`, its hosts are RECURSIVE (subtask 4). The same on gfortran |
| `recurhost.f90` | Internal procedures of RECURSIVE hosts (Phase 103, subtask 4): each activation's own frame variables, CHARACTER variable, and dummies reached by its internal procedures after deeper activations have returned, by the FP the host passes as a hidden argument; a sibling passing it on; a RECURSIVE function's RESULT variable and dummy set and read by its internal procedure. The same on gfortran |
| `interfaces.f90` | Interface blocks (Phase 103, subtask 5): a main program's block describing four external procedures the file defines (their references checked, a CHARACTER function typed by its body, a CHARACTER\*(\*) dummy), a body describing its own dummy procedure with a nested block, and an internal procedure's block describing a function (with RESULT, which its definition hasn't) passed with no EXTERNAL statement to a subroutine whose block makes its dummy a function. The same on gfortran |
| `optional.f90` | Keyword arguments, OPTIONAL dummies, PRESENT, and INTENT (Phase 103, subtask 6): calls through an interface block with arguments left out, given by keyword in any order, or both; a function's OPTIONAL dummies; an INTENT(OUT) adjustable array; an OPTIONAL adjustable array left out; an internal procedure passing its own OPTIONAL dummy on, absent or not; an internal procedure asking PRESENT of its host's dummy. The same on gfortran |
| `generics.f90` | Generic interfaces (Phase 103, subtask 7): SWAP's three subroutines told apart by type, one called by keyword; TWICE's three functions told apart by kind; NORM's two told apart by rank; MAX extended to LOGICAL values while MAX(3, 7) is still the intrinsic's; an internal procedure using its host's SWAP and adding a specific of its own. The same on gfortran |
| `operators.f90` | Defined operators and assignment (Phase 103, subtask 8): binary `.DIST.` on points and `.SD.` binding loosest, unary `.INV.` binding tightest, `+` extended to LOGICAL operands, `//` to a CHARACTER and an INTEGER, `.AND.` to INTEGERs (taking over VAX FORTRAN's bitwise meaning) while `3 + 4` stays Fortran's, ASSIGNMENT(=) of a LOGICAL to a CHARACTER variable, and an internal procedure using its host's operators. The same on gfortran |
| `hostopt.f90` | The optimizer beside internal procedures (Phase 103, subtask 9): loops holding a host variable in static storage, a host's dummy reached through its cell, a RECURSIVE host's frame variable, and a host's OPTIONAL dummy, each changed or asked about by an internal procedure the loop calls. The same on gfortran |
| `numbers.f90` | Phase 103's features together (subtask 9): `.GCD.` (a RECURSIVE function with RESULT, also used through an interface block in another external function), `.LCM.`, and `.CHOOSE.` as defined operators, left to right; a generic SHOW for INTEGERs and REALs with OPTIONAL widths, by keyword or not; internal procedures filling and summing the host's array for the host's DO variable. The same on gfortran |
| `autohost.f90` | An internal procedure of a host with AUTOMATIC variables (Phase 103, subtask 4), reading and changing them in the host's frame, and a variable format expression in the internal procedure reading one. DEC's AUTOMATIC and `<W>` keep it from gfortran |
| `allocs.f90` | Allocatable arrays (Phase 104, subtask 2): ALLOCATE with bounds known only when the program runs, ALLOCATED before and after, elements, whole arrays, and sections of one and two dimensions, SIZE, LBOUND, UBOUND, and SHAPE, a sum by DIM=, DEALLOCATE and ALLOCATE again with other bounds, a zero-sized array, a whole allocatable array passed to an explicit-shape dummy, an internal procedure allocating and filling its host's, a RECURSIVE function with one of its own at each level. The same on gfortran |
| `allocstat.f90` | Allocation status (Phase 104, subtask 3): STAT= on ALLOCATE and DEALLOCATE, succeeding and failing, into an INTEGER(2) and an array element; a statement stopping at its first failure; a zero-sized array; a subprogram's arrays deallocated at every return (an early RETURN, END, a function's value, an alternate return computed from the array, either of two entry points) and so unallocated at each call; a SAVE'd one kept; a host's array allocated by its internal procedure, freed at the host's return; an internal procedure's own; a recursive function's at each level. The same on gfortran |
| `autolen.f90` | CHARACTER lengths that aren't constant (Phase 104, subtask 4b): a dummy argument's, the first N characters of its actual, whatever N becomes after entry; automatic scalars and arrays in both forms, from a dummy, a common block, LEN, and MAX; by element and substring, in output lists, passed to passed-length dummies, reached by an internal procedure; lengths of zero and less; one at each level of a recursion; an ENTRY with the dummies in another order; ten thousand calls. The same on gfortran |
| `rtemps.f90` | Array temporaries of a size known only when the program runs (Phase 104, subtask 4c): a reversal and a shift read both ways through a temporary, a WHERE whose mask the construct's first assignment changes, a vector subscript of the target's own array (with a constructor stored straight in, and with an array expression), constructors of a run-time size in reductions, in an expression, in a logical IF, a CASE construct's selector, and a DO WHILE's condition, a CHARACTER array of a run-time length reversed and given constructors, a CHARACTER function's value and a concatenation of a run-time length in array expressions and an output list, MERGE of run-time lengths, a temporary of 80,000 bytes (from the heap), and an assignment through a temporary 6,001 times in one call (the stack given back each time). The same on gfortran |
| `shaped.f90` | Assumed-shape dummy arguments (Phase 104, subtask 5a): internal procedures, and external ones through interface blocks, given whole arrays (of constant bounds, adjustable, automatic, and allocatable) and sections, one of no elements, with any strides, backward too, of one and two dimensions, a row of a matrix among them; their own lower bounds; SIZE, LBOUND, UBOUND, and SUM of them, whole-array assignment and elements written back to the caller's array; a CHARACTER(LEN=\*) one; one passed on to another, whole and as a section, by a recursive function to itself; an OPTIONAL one left out. The same on gfortran |
| `shapes.f90` | Assumed-shape dummies, further (Phase 104, subtask 5a): a lower bound that is a dummy argument, an automatic array of SIZE of one, an ENTRY with the dummies in another order, an internal procedure reading its host's, INTENT(IN) and INTENT(INOUT) ones of rank two given sections stepping both ways in both dimensions, DOT_PRODUCT of two. The same on gfortran |
| `shapeargs.f90` | Assumed-shape dummies given values (Phase 104, subtask 5b): an array expression, a vector-subscripted section, a section in parentheses, an elemental function's value, and a constructor, each through a temporary; one of a size known only when the program runs; a dummy's own lower bound on an expression; substrings of a section described where they are, and of a vector-subscripted section and a concatenation through temporaries; OPTIONAL assumed-shape and explicit-shape dummies passed on, absent or not; a generic name with specifics of ranks 1 and 2; a function given an expression a thousand times in a loop. The same on gfortran |
| `seqargs.f90` | Sections and expressions to dummies that aren't assumed-shape (Phase 104, subtask 6): contiguous sections passed where they are; strided, row, and reversed sections copied in and back; expressions and vector-subscripted sections copied in only; CHARACTER sections, substrings of them, and a concatenation; an assumed-shape array and its sections tested when the program runs, both ways, also as a run-time format and an internal file; an allocatable array's row; an alternate return and a function after a copy; a row of 20,000 elements through the heap; a dynamic string beside a copied section. The same on gfortran |
| `seqvms.f90` | The same, VMS's side: an assumed-shape array as ENCODE's and DECODE's buffer, copied or not; LIB$STAT_VM's bytes unchanged by twenty heap temporaries |
| `values.f90` | Array-valued functions of a shape known when compiling (Phase 104, subtask 7a): an external one through an interface body, internal ones of rank 1 and 2, a recursive one with RESULT, a CHARACTER one; values in expressions, reductions, MATMUL, WHERE, IF, output lists, as arguments to old and assumed-shape dummies, assigned to their own argument, through a dummy procedure and a generic name, and called a thousand times. The same on gfortran |
| `ramps.f90` | Array-valued functions whose value's shape is known only when the program runs (Phase 104, subtask 7b), made by the function: an external one through an interface body, an internal one with bounds from SIZE of an assumed-shape dummy, one of rank 2, one with a lower bound of 0, one of its host's variable, a recursive one with RESULT using its own value; values of no elements; in expressions, reductions, WHERE, IF, output lists and an implied DO list, as arguments to old and assumed-shape dummies, assigned to a section, and called a thousand times. The same on gfortran |
| `rampvms.f90` | The same, VMS's side: LIB$STAT_VM's bytes unchanged by thousands of values given back, in assignments, an implied DO list calling the function at each pass, a logical IF, an arithmetic IF, a computed GO TO, a CALL with alternate returns, a recursive function's references to itself, values past the stack's limit for temporaries, and CHARACTER values of a run-time length, scalars and arrays (subtask 7c), one in an implied DO list; dynamic strings come from LIB$SGET1_DD's own zone, which LIB$STAT_VM's count leaves out |
| `madetext.f90` | CHARACTER values of a length known only when the program runs (Phase 104, subtask 7c): a scalar made as a dynamic string, in concatenations, LEN, a comparison, SELECT CASE, an implied DO list, an argument to a passed-length dummy, assigned to a substring; a recursive one with RESULT down to no characters; an internal one whose length is SIZE of a dummy; arrays of such a length, internal and external; ENTRY in functions whose value is an array of a known shape, of a shape known only at run time, and a string of a length known only then; a string made a thousand times. The same on gfortran |
| `autos.f90` | Automatic arrays (Phase 104, subtask 4a): bounds from dummy arguments, a common block, SIZE, LBOUND, UBOUND, LEN, and MAX; whole and by element, in output lists, passed to an explicit-shape dummy, reached by an internal procedure; zero-sized ones; one at each level of a recursion; an ENTRY with the dummies in another order; ten thousand calls, so that each return must give its storage back. The same on gfortran |
| `allocvms.f90` | Allocation status as VMS sees it (Phase 104, subtask 3): STAT='s FOR numbers (301, 302, 41 for an array past 2\*\*31 - 1 bytes); the same failures signaled without STAT=, each made its routine's value by LIB$SIG_TO_RET; a routine unwound with its array allocated, whose next call allocates it again; LIB$STAT_VM's bytes unchanged by a recursion whose levels' arrays their returns free. VMS's own, so not in `compare.py` |
| `modules/mixed` | Both source forms in one program: `mixed.f90` and `report.f90` free, `fill.for` fixed, and `limits.inc`, INCLUDEd by both forms, written to read the same way in either |
| `modules/shortlist` | VMS's shorter argument list (Phase 103, subtask 6): a FORTRAN-77 caller in a file of its own leaving OPTS's last OPTIONAL dummies out altogether, and a null argument; PRESENT tells by the argument count, and OPTS passes them on to its internal procedure as absent. DEC's null argument keeps it from gfortran |
